title: Government Provides ₹10.66 Crore Financial Assistance to 457 Beneficiaries under Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Inter-Caste Marriages
body_text:
The Central Government has informed the Rajya Sabha that the Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages and the Dr. Ambedkar National Relief to the Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes Victims of Atrocities Scheme were merged with the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 , with effect from 31 March 2023 , to avoid duplication in the implementation of schemes.
This information was provided by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale , in a written reply to Shri Raghav Chadha in the Rajya Sabha today.
The Minister submitted that under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 , Central assistance is provided to State Governments and Union Territory Administrations adding that the scheme is implemented by the respective State Governments/UT Administrations, and the responsibility for its effective implementation rests with them.
The Dr. Ambedkar Foundation continued to process and provide financial assistance in pending cases pertaining to the Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages that arose prior to the merger. Accordingly, financial assistance amounting to ₹ 10.66 crore has been released to 457 beneficiaries .
The year-wise details show that 68 beneficiaries received financial assistance during 2023-24, 11 beneficiaries during 2024-25 and 378 beneficiaries during 2025-26 , taking the total number of beneficiaries to 457 during the three-year period.

enrichment.summary: The Central Government informed the Rajya Sabha that the Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages was merged with the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, effective 31 March 2023, to avoid duplication. Despite the merger, the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation continued processing pending inter-caste marriage cases, releasing ₹10.66 crore to 457 beneficiaries over 2023-24 to 2025-26 (68, 11, and 378 beneficiaries respectively). The information was shared by Minister of State Ramdas Athawale in a written reply.
enrichment.context:
The Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages was launched to incentivize inter-caste marriages, particularly those involving a Scheduled Caste partner, as a means of promoting social integration and combating caste-based discrimination in India. It provided a one-time financial incentive to eligible couples. Similarly, the Dr. Ambedkar National Relief to SC/ST Victims of Atrocities Scheme provided relief to victims of caste-based atrocities. Both schemes have now been subsumed into the broader Centrally Sponsored Scheme for implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights (PCR) Act, 1955 and the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, which is the primary legal-cum-welfare framework for protecting SC/ST communities from discrimination and violence, and is implemented through state governments and UT administrations with central financial assistance.

This rationalization reflects a broader governmental push toward scheme convergence to reduce administrative duplication and improve delivery efficiency, a trend seen across several ministries. For UPSC aspirants, this development is relevant to understanding India's institutional architecture for SC/ST welfare, the interplay between central schemes and state implementation responsibilities, and the continuing relevance of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's legacy in contemporary social justice policy, especially concerning annihilation of caste and social integration through inter-caste marriage as envisioned in Ambedkar's writings.
